author: mmikolajcz
title: fusings_gpu pooling_f32_scale fp16_scale_out fails GPU unit test tolerance check
signature: gpu unit tests fusion pooling scale fp16 difference between val ref and val opt exceeds tolerance|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 fails numerical tolerance comparison in fusion_test_common.hpp

key_errors: C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\openvino\src\plugins\intel_gpu\tests\unit\fusions\fusion_test_common.hpp(90): error: The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is 3.0517578125e-05, which exceeds tolerance, where val_ref[i] evaluates to -0.04473876953125, val_opt[i] evaluates to -0.044769287109375, tolerance evaluates to 9.9999997473787516e-06 (i = 14)
root_cause: This is a known recurring flaky GPU unit test (fp16_scale_out) comparing the fused vs non-fused pooling+scale kernel output against a tight absolute fp16 tolerance (1e-5). The fp16 rounding error for this particular test case straddles the tolerance boundary, so the test intermittently passes or fails depending on scheduling/ordering-induced floating point variance on the GPU runner, independent of code changes. The PR behind this merge-queue run (#38762, NGramHashFunction CPU op) does not touch GPU fusion code, confirming no causal link between the change and the failure.
reproduction_steps: Run on a Windows GPU runner: ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe --gtest_filter=fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 (may require several repetitions to reproduce the borderline tolerance failure).
recommended_actions: Loosen the fp16 comparison tolerance for fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out in fusion_test_common.hpp, or convert the fp16 absolute tolerance check to a relative/ULP-based comparison
Mark the test as known-flaky (skip/disable) until the tolerance is fixed, to avoid repeatedly blocking the merge queue
Approve the pending rerun_search_string proposal for this pattern so the workflow rerunner can automatically retry it
prevention_strategies: Use relative or ULP-based tolerance comparisons for fp16 reference-vs-optimized kernel tests instead of a fixed absolute epsilon, since fp16 rounding error scales with magnitude and a single flat tolerance will always have borderline cases near the threshold.
historical_context: This exact signature has now recurred 5 times in the last ~13 hours (first seen 2026-11-13T23:41:12Z, most recently 2026-11-14T07:13:04Z before this run), affecting unrelated PRs #39011, #39548, #39826, and #38855 in addition to this one (#38762). None of the affected PRs touch GPU fusion code, confirming this is an environment/test-tolerance flake rather than a regression.
